fallback.title: Not sure
tips: Scan one item at a time.

recyclable.label: Recyclable
recyclable.title: Dry Recyclables
steps: Put it in the dry-waste bin or give it to a kabadiwala or recycler.
accepted: Aluminium beverage cans & tin food tins
notAccepted: Greasy pizza boxes with melted cheese
Thin single-use plastic films / grocery pouches
recyclable.tips: Rinse with leftover dishwater to remove liquids. Crush cans and flatten boxes to conserve bin volume.
recyclable.sdgFact: Recycling reduces demand for new raw material taken from forests and land.
recyclable.guideFact: Every metric ton of recycled paper preserves 17 mature trees and avoids 4,000 kW·h of electrical energy.

organic.label: Organic
organic.title: Wet Compostable Organic Waste
steps: Put it in the wet-waste bin or a compost pit.
accepted: Fruit peels, citrus rinds & vegetable trimmings
Coffee grounds, filter paper & tea bags
Garden leaves, cut flowers & dead plant stems
notAccepted: Synthetic tea bags with nylon mesh
organic.tips: Composting aerobically halts methane production and creates nutrient-rich humus for urban gardening.
organic.sdgFact: Compost returns nutrients to soil instead of rotting in landfills.
organic.guideFact: Organic soil matter restores subterranean microbiome diversity and increases moisture retention by up to 20%.

ewaste.label: E-Waste
ewaste.title: Electronic & Digital Waste
steps: Don't put it in household waste.
Hand it to an authorised e-waste collector or a take-back counter.
accepted: Charging cords, USB cables & power adapters
notAccepted: Swollen or leaking lithium-ion pouch cells (treat as Hazardous)
ewaste.tips: Back up and factory reset devices. Never toss e-waste in domestic dumpsters where metals crush and spark fires.
ewaste.sdgFact: Toxic metals from dumped electronics can leak into soil and harm land ecosystems.
ewaste.guideFact: Recycling 1 million mobile phones recovers 16,000 kg of copper, 350 kg of silver, and 34 kg of gold.

hazardous.label: Hazardous
hazardous.title: Hazardous & Chemical Waste
steps: Don't burn, flush or mix it.
Give it to a hazardous-waste collection point.
hazardous.tips: Retain in original marked containers with safety labels visible. Store upright out of reach of children.
hazardous.sdgFact: Chemicals and batteries that reach the ground contaminate soil and the life that depends on it.
hazardous.guideFact: A single cadmium battery can contaminate 600,000 liters of groundwater—preventing dumping halts toxic soil sterility.

general.label: General / Non-recyclable
general.title: General / Non-Recyclable Residuals
steps: Wrap it and put it in the general dry non-recyclable bin.
accepted: Multi-layer laminated snack wrappers & foil pouches
Used facial tissues, cotton swabs & sanitary napkins
Broken porcelain mugs & drinking glass shards (wrapped)
general.tips: Tie trash liners tightly to prevent lightweight plastic fragments from dispersing onto natural wildlife reserves.
general.sdgFact: Waste left on open land damages soil and habitats, so proper disposal protects them.
general.guideFact: Responsible containment shields open grasslands, rivers, and wildlife habitats from fatal microplastic ingestion.
